Chapter 6: God’s Holiness—The Center of His Being
Holiness. It’s one of those words that can feel far away—maybe even a little intimidating, right? For a lot of us, it brings to mind something untouchable, or impossibly pure. But here’s something worth pausing over: at the very center of our journey to know God, we find that His holiness isn’t just another quality—it’s the core of who He is.
Imagine yourself walking through a quiet forest at dawn. Everything’s still, the air is sharp and clear, and every leaf seems to glow with an almost unexplainable light. In that moment, you feel like you’re in the presence of something different, something that demands your respect and your attention. That’s what holiness feels like—not just a definition, but an experience.
Most people don’t realize this, but God’s holiness is what makes Him completely unique. Sure, it’s about moral perfection, but it’s also about being set apart—utterly unlike anything else in all creation. God’s holiness means He’s above and beyond anything ordinary or common. That’s why, all through history, when people have truly encountered God, their first response is usually awe, sometimes fear, and a deep humility.
Let me share a story. There was someone who, for years, thought faith was just about following rules. But then, one day, in the middle of a simple prayer, they suddenly became aware of God’s presence—of His holiness. It was overwhelming, but also comforting. And in that moment, they realized holiness isn’t about being good enough; it’s about being drawn in by the One who is completely other.
That’s the turning point: holiness isn’t something we achieve, it’s something we receive. When you catch even a glimpse of God’s holiness, it humbles you—but it also lifts you up. You begin to understand that you’re loved by a God who is both infinitely pure and endlessly gracious. And that realization? It changes everything. Suddenly, life feels more serious, but there’s also a new kind of joy. The call to be holy isn’t some heavy burden—it’s an invitation to share in God’s own life.
Now, maybe you’ve struggled with the whole idea of holiness, worrying it might make God seem distant or harsh. But here’s the twist: it’s actually the opposite. God’s holiness is what makes His love so powerful, His mercy so surprising, and His presence so incredibly life-changing. When you draw near to God’s holiness, you find yourself changed—not because you worked harder, but because of grace.
